archetype.name: Dual-Threat (efficiency-first)
archetype.definition: A run-threat quarterback whose legs bend the defense and buy time, and whose arm this year turned a modest number of dropbacks into the most yards per attempt in the league.

report.headline: League-best efficiency on low volume, now on hold behind thumb surgery
report.take:
Jackson is the same player he has been for years, a quarterback who forces defenses to account for his legs and then punishes them with timing throws, but this season the passing efficiency climbed back to his 2019 and 2024 level. His 9.97 yards per attempt and 10.63 adjusted net yards per dropback both rank 1st of 49, his 0.354 EPA per dropback ranks 3rd, and his 8.29 CPOE also ranks 3rd. Last year he dropped to 0.126 EPA per play and 1.8 CPOE. That was the outlier, not this.

The volume tells a different story. He averaged only 19.4 attempts a game in a Ravens offense that passes less than situation predicts, so his 193.4 passing yards a game ranks 26th even though he leads the league in yards per attempt. The efficiency is broad rather than one fluke split. Short throws produced 0.504 EPA with five of his six touchdowns, intermediate throws 0.812, and deep throws 0.745. Zay Flowers was the engine at 1.359 EPA per target, and the left and middle of the field were both strong. The legs still matter too: 28.8 rushing yards a game ranks 5th, and his 10 scrambles turned into 6 first downs.

The numbers hide how little of the season there was. He played four real games. Week 4 ended at 52% of snaps, he missed Weeks 5-7, and he took two snaps in Week 8 at Buffalo before going down again. The last-three line includes that one-throw game, so its per-game volume is meaningless, though its rates show his best football came in Weeks 3 and 4. There are soft spots too. Third down produced 0.01 EPA with a 34.8% conversion rate, because he faced 9.2 yards to go on average. The red zone came in at -0.07 EPA despite four touchdowns. His 16.5% bad-throw rate ranks 35th of 42, a career-long trait that his completion numbers have papered over before.

Now he is on injured reserve after surgery on his right thumb, his throwing hand, listed fourth on the depth chart, with an estimated return of December 13. He has told teammates he plans to come back this season. Tyler Huntley is also on IR, and Joe Fagnano started Week 9. The open question is no longer how good he is. It is whether he returns in time to matter and whether the thumb lets him throw with the same touch.

strengths.title: Yards per attempt leads the league
strengths.body: He gains chunks on every kind of throw. That is not just deep shots: his short game alone returned 0.504 EPA per attempt on 49 throws with a 79.6% completion rate. The 2024 season (8.8 YPA, 2nd) shows this ceiling is real for him. It is likely sustainable when healthy, though a 97-attempt sample flatters the exact figure.

strengths.title: Accuracy over expected rebounded
strengths.body: His CPOE jumped 6.5 points from last season to 8.29, 3rd in the league, the best mark of his career. Some of that is the offense creating easy completions, and his bad-throw rate has not improved. Expect it to settle toward his 3-4.5 range from his best years rather than hold at 8, especially coming off thumb surgery.

strengths.title: Legs still move the chains
strengths.body: He ranks 5th in rushing yards per game, and the scrambles averaged 0.48 EPA, so the extended plays pay for themselves. His pressure-to-sack rate of 28% is far better than last year's, and sacks on 6.7% of dropbacks is better than the league average. The running is a career-long constant. The question is only how freely he runs after the injury.

concerns.title: Throwing-hand surgery and availability
concerns.body: He is on IR after surgery on his right thumb, with a December 13 return date that is an estimate. He has already left two of his five games early. A thumb on the throwing hand is exactly the kind of injury that can sap ball placement on return, and his bad-throw rate was already among the league's worst.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone lag
concerns.body: His dropbacks are excellent on early downs but stall when the field shrinks or the distance grows. Third down produced 0.01 EPA with a 34.8% conversion rate, and the red zone ran negative despite four touchdowns. Long yardage explains part of it (9.2 yards to go on average). On 23 and 15 plays, these are warnings rather than verdicts.

concerns.title: Low volume caps the box score
concerns.body: A run-leaning team that passes 3.6 points under expectation, plus early exits, holds him to 19.4 attempts a game. That is why his yardage ranks 26th despite the league's best yards per attempt. This is role, not a flaw, but it limits raw output even when he is healthy.

trend.note: The efficiency climbed through September: Weeks 3 and 4 were his cleanest games, with CPOE of 9.2 and 11.3 and nearly 12 EPA each. Then injuries cut Week 4 short, cost him three games and ended Week 8 after one throw.

nextGame.headline: Jackson is on IR; Week 10 belongs to Baltimore's backups
nextGame.body:
Jackson will not play against the Chargers. He is on injured reserve after thumb surgery with a December 13 estimated return. The matchup would have suited him. Los Angeles ranks 29th in deep-pass EPA allowed and 22nd in explosive-pass rate, and that is where his 0.745 EPA on deep throws lives. The Chargers' offense is the league's worst by EPA, which is why the Book sets a 38.5 total with Baltimore favored by 5.5 even without him.

The availability that matters is in Baltimore's quarterback room. Tyler Huntley, who played 74% of snaps while Jackson was out, is also on IR, so Joe Fagnano, who started Week 9, is in line again. On the other side, Justin Herbert is questionable with a finger injury that avoided a fracture, and Ladd McConkey is day to day with back spasms. For Jackson himself, the only relevant news this week is any change in his own recovery timeline.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers' leaky deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles allows 1.058 EPA on deep passes, 29th in the league, and that is the area where Jackson did much of his damage. It is a vulnerability to remember if these teams meet again. This week it is a test of whether a backup can exploit it.

keyMatchups.title: Low-total, run-heavy script
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers' offense ranks last in EPA, last in success rate and last in pass rate over expected. The game projects as slow and low-scoring. That limits passing volume for whoever starts at quarterback in Baltimore.

keyMatchups.title: Baltimore's thin quarterback depth
keyMatchups.body: With Jackson and Huntley both on IR, the offense runs through the third option. That shapes the team Jackson returns to, and how much the season depends on his timeline.

nextGame.watch: Any update on Jackson's recovery, whether he resumes throwing or opens a practice window ahead of the December 13 target.

restOfSeason.body:
Everything depends on the thumb. If he returns around mid-December, he has a few regular-season games left. Expect his rushing and decision-making to hold, since those have been constants for years. Expect the passing efficiency to come down from league-best levels: an 8.29 CPOE and nearly 10 yards per attempt on 97 throws were partly a hot sample, and a surgically repaired throwing hand is likely to cost some placement early. A return closer to his 2023-2025 form (around 8 to 8.5 yards per attempt) is the reasonable baseline. The team's run-first lean keeps attempts modest.

Project roughly 180-240 passing yards and 1-2 touchdowns a game when active, with 20-40 rushing yards. That rushing range has a softer floor if Baltimore asks him to protect the hand. The realistic risk is not decline but absence: a later return, a cautious ramp-up, or no return at all if the team's season slips away while he is out.
swingFactors: Thumb recovery and actual return date
Throwing accuracy in first games back
Baltimore's playoff standing when he is cleared

confidence.note: Only four real games played, followed by throwing-hand surgery with an uncertain return.
